Battery marginal energy-action displacement, 2023-2025

This report estimates matched offer- and bid-side counterfactuals conditional on a battery occupying the active-side margin. It removes the full accepted volume of that battery BMU and fills the shortfall from unused classified non-battery BOD actions beyond the observed battery margin. Offer results remain the primary analysis; Section 11 restores the directly comparable energy-bid analysis with its cashflow sign stated explicitly.

How to read the result. The gap is simply replacement non-battery offer − battery offer. A positive value means the battery avoided a more expensive offer. No bid-price sign conversion is involved.
Boundary. This holds the submitted national BOD ladder and requirement fixed. It does not model network constraints, operational feasibility, rebidding, or rerun the complete PAR/flagging System Price process.

Identity audit. T_KEMB-1 (Pivot Power Kemsley) was corrected from LOAD RESPONSE to BATTERY and excluded from the non-battery replacement pool before the final counterfactual was rerun.

Visual guide: the result in three pictures

1. Which side has the favourable price?

Each line joins the battery's accepted-action VWAP to the volume-matched replacement-ladder VWAP. On offers, value appears when the red replacement point is more expensive than the blue battery point. On bids, value appears when the blue battery point is higher because NESO receives more money back.

2. Is the result common or confined to a few extreme events?

The bars classify the exact full-BMU accepted-action cost comparison—not only the final marginal price gap. A growing green share means the result is becoming more prevalent rather than being produced by a small tail.

3. Which technologies are immediately behind the battery?

Each cell reports that technology's share of all identified marginal replacements in the year and the exact benefit per removed battery MWh. Frequency identifies the common alternative; colour and the £/MWh number identify economic intensity. The technology is the final action reached, not necessarily every action contributing replacement volume.

1. Main result: full accepted battery-BMU volume removed

The dot is the median and the bar is the IQR. P95 is printed above each point so the upper tail is visible without a logarithmic axis.

Headline offer-side results.
  • 2023: median £0.25/MWh; IQR £0.00–£1.40; P95 £4.40; positive in 55.1% of identified observations.
  • 2024: median £0.35/MWh; IQR £0.00–£0.90; P95 £2.75; positive in 70.4%.
  • 2025: median £0.72/MWh; IQR £0.25–£1.75; P95 £7.07; positive in 92.7%.

The strongest change is prevalence: by 2025 the middle 50% of observations is entirely above zero, rather than the result depending only on a small upper tail.

The per-action marginal-price proxy columns equal the final price gap multiplied by the removed BMU MWh. They are not annual consumer savings and are not additive across overlapping leave-one-unit-out counterfactuals.

2. Crude savings estimates at multiple levels

Two monetary measures are reported. The accepted-action reconstruction sums each replacement BOD tranche's volume times its submitted offer price, then subtracts every accepted battery pair's ISPStack volume times its recorded original offer price. The marginal proxy applies only the final marginal price gap to all removed MWh. Their difference captures the fact that the battery BMU can have inframarginal accepted pairs priced below its marginal offer.

Three-year avoided-cost estimate. Across 2023–2025, the accepted-action reconstruction gives £93,943 when separate leave-one-BMU experiments are summed, or £84,266 after co-marginal observations are tie-adjusted. The preferred tie-adjusted headline comprises £19,836 from climbing the replacement ladder and £64,430 from replacing lower-priced accepted battery pairs. The narrower marginal-price proxies are £27,779 and £20,898.
These are not GB consumer savings. They cover only battery-marginal offer observations and hold the BOD ladder fixed. Raw totals sum separate leave-one-BMU-out experiments and can overlap when several batteries are marginal in one SP. Tie-adjusted totals give each SP total weight one and are the more conservative occurrence-based statistic.

Price reconstruction audit. Pair-level accepted original prices were available for 100.0% of identified full-BMU observations and 100.0% of their accepted MWh. Rows without complete price coverage fall back to marginal offer times volume and are flagged in the observation-level CSV.

3. Visualising the offer-stack displacement

Each panel ranks battery-marginal observations by the submitted battery offer. The blue line is the observed battery offer and the red line is the non-battery offer reached after removing the full accepted battery-BMU volume. The shaded distance is the paired displacement. This is an empirical conditional ladder across periods—not one literal national supply curve.

In conventional supply-and-demand language, adding BESS shifts total available supply outward/right, while reducing the residual quantity required from non-battery offers. The graph directly shows the associated downward movement in the marginal offer.

4. Narrower robustness: marginal accepted slice removed

This keeps the earlier unit-row estimand. Its similarity to the full-BMU result shows whether the estimated price distance is driven by very small marginal fragments.

11. Integrated bid-side counterpart

This repeats the same static marginal-event experiment for energy bids. The full accepted volume of a battery BMU at the bid-side margin is removed and replaced from unused non-battery BOD bids at or below the battery bid, ordered from highest to lowest. The reported gap is battery bid minus replacement bid. A positive value means the battery would have paid more money back to NESO than the replacement action.

Boundary. These are energy bids from the canonical soFlag=False stack. Utilised and reversed System Bids are not included, and no replacement Offer is attached to a reversed export. The result therefore should not be interpreted as Modo's system-bid accounting.
Bid-side annual medians.
  • 2023: median benefit £0.80/MWh; IQR £0.00–£2.40; positive in 63.2% of identified observations.
  • 2024: median benefit £0.42/MWh; IQR £0.00–£1.49; positive in 61.8%.
  • 2025: median benefit £0.84/MWh; IQR £0.22–£2.00; positive in 90.1%.

Bid-side avoided-cost reconstruction

For positive bids this is money received by NESO. The accepted-pair reconstruction compares the battery BMU's actual volume-weighted bid receipts with the cost-to-SO value of the replacement bid ladder. Across the three-year window the raw leave-one-BMU sum is £89,869; after co-marginal ties are weighted, it is £72,604.

Only 13 of 6,091 identified full-BMU observations have a materially negative exact benefit, but the battery bid itself can still be negative. The comparison below therefore distinguishes paying NESO more than the alternative from always paying NESO.

Recommended interpretation

Conditional on a battery setting the active-side margin, the analysis estimates how much farther NESO would have needed to move through the submitted non-battery stack if that battery BMU's accepted volume were absent. On offers, positive values are avoided replacement expenditure. On bids, positive values are additional receipts retained because the battery bid is higher. Both are transparent mechanical displacement results, not market-equilibrium causal effects.
